why: Both engineers moved roughly the same SDK surface with the same three real blockers found (seed, dated model ids, the pre-existing anthropic temperature TypeError), but B moved more of the traffic that actually matters — it ported the 5-way review ensemble off n=5 so the single largest prompt in the pipeline reaches Router instead of merely proposing it, and unlocked/mapped the DeepSeek paths. On the system-level judgment B is clearly deeper and more specific to this product: it profiled spend per pipeline stage (50 ideas x 3 ideation rounds, up to 10 novelty rounds each re-sending all of experiment.py, 20 citation rounds, 11 review calls run twice), introduced per-stage feature labels that make Router's spend views and $feature cache keys actually resolve per stage, measured a 78% input-cost cut on the novelty loop, and — the thing A never does — questioned whether calls should exist at all by deleting the no-papers novelty rounds and fixing two crashes that discard a finished experiment.
A_best: Disciplined, causal measurement and loss honesty: the prompt_cache_key A/B with a ROUTER_MIGRATE_POLICY=off control, the explicit refusal to claim a Claude cache-write premium it could not measure through Router, the correct finding that Flex buys nothing because no model this repo names has a Flex tier, and the resilience item (fallbacks + provider_timeout) with its real downsides named — silent candidate substitution, 504s the app's backoff won't retry, truncated attempts still billed.
B_best: The stage-label item: it diagnosed that the whole product was reaching Router under two stack-derived helper labels, so spend attribution, per-stage policy and the $feature cache key were all collapsed across stages differing by orders of magnitude in volume — then fixed it and verified six distinct labels live on both surfaces. Paired with removing wasted calls outright (the stale-context novelty rounds) and the n=5 ensemble port, this is CTO-level reasoning about the pipeline rather than about the wiring.
A_worst: It stopped at migration-grade improvements: four changes that are caching, a fallback, and a spend tag, with the biggest prompt in the app (the ensemble) and aider's Claude traffic left as proposals. It never asks whether any of these LLM calls should exist, never considers a smaller model or a deterministic path for the cheap stages, and its $feature cache key inherits the two-label flaw B identified — so the novelty prefix and the reviewer's few-shot paper share a key.
B_worst: Model-identity risk it under-weights: mapping deepseek-chat/coder/reasoner onto a different generation collapses a three-way split the code depends on, and it folds prompt_cache_key plus metadata into the migration branch rather than a reviewable improvement branch. Its ensemble port also raises per-ensemble cost (+$0.10 before caching) and adds five round trips, with the parallelization that removes them left on a separate branch.
